name: Copernicus’s heliocentric planetary system
summary: Copernicus's short Commentariolus, known by 1514, described a system in which Earth spins daily and circles the Sun, ideas later developed in De revolutionibus.
description: A planetary system in which Earth rotates and travels around the Sun, outlined in the Commentariolus before the later De revolutionibus.
tier_reason: The reorganised planetary framework supports subsequent astronomical modelling and celestial mechanics over generations.

impact.note: Changed what educated societies took the world to be; later astronomy and physics over many generations stood on a moving Earth.

why: Copernicus objected that Ptolemy's equant broke the rule of uniform circular motion and sought a more coherent arrangement of the planets.
